title: August 23–September 12, 1897
scope_note: Expansion in progress: 51 sourced items across August 23–September 12, 1897. The widened window preserves the accepted September 6–12 record set by reference and begins adding documented lead-up material before the Palace Square mass meeting. Sparse early dates remain sparse until source-facing Hawaiian is recovered; historical attention, not a quota, determines what survives.

items.voice_actor: Joseph Heleluhe, on behalf of Liliʻuokalani
items.english_close: You two are to confer together.
items.feed_rendering: Kaulia and Kalauokalani: confer with each other. Move this together.
items.voice_evidence: The preserved Hawaiian is an explicit instruction to the two anti-annexation leaders to confer rather than operate separately. The scholarly source identifies the Ebbitt House letter as from Joseph Heleluhe on behalf of Liliʻuokalani.
items.source_label: Noenoe K. Silva, Aloha Betrayed, quoting the Sept. 1, 1897 Ebbitt House letter later published by ʻAʻima Nāwahī
items.translation_basis: Silva quotes the Hawaiian letter and supplies English translation and attribution context. Publication timing in Ke Aloha Aina is not resolved here, so no publication date is inferred.

items.voice_actor: Joseph Heleluhe, on behalf of Liliʻuokalani
items.hawaiian: e kahea ia la hoi ka Papa hooko a me ka Aha Kuwaena o na Hui a elua
items.english_close: Call the executive board and central committee of the two organizations together.
items.feed_rendering: Call both organizations' leadership together. Settle the petition together.
items.voice_evidence: The letter specifically directs the executive and central leadership of both organizations to be convened. In the surrounding passage, that joint meeting is to decide the heading under which the lāhui will protest annexation.
items.source_label: Noenoe K. Silva, Aloha Betrayed, quoting the Sept. 1, 1897 Ebbitt House letter later published by ʻAʻima Nāwahī
items.translation_basis: Silva quotes and translates the historical correspondence. Feed wording compresses the supported coordination instruction without treating it as verbatim speech.

items.voice_actor: Joseph Heleluhe, on behalf of Liliʻuokalani
items.hawaiian: a iwaena oia halawai ana e noonoo ai oukou i ke poo o ka ka lahui kue no ka hoohui aina, a malalo la hoi oia poo e kakau inoa mai ai na makaaina aloha aina a pau loa
items.english_close: At that meeting, consider the heading for the lāhui's protest against annexation, and under that heading let all aloha ʻāina makaʻāinana sign their names.
items.feed_rendering: Agree on one heading for the lāhui's protest. Then let the aloha ʻāina sign under it.
items.voice_evidence: This is a distinct operational instruction inside the letter: unify the petition's heading and gather the lāhui's signatures beneath it. It shows the petition as coordinated political work rather than a spontaneous document.
items.source_label: Noenoe K. Silva, Aloha Betrayed, quoting the Sept. 1, 1897 Ebbitt House letter later published by ʻAʻima Nāwahī
items.translation_basis: Silva preserves the Hawaiian passage and English translation. The feed rendering stays close to the petition-coordination action in the source.

items.voice_actor: Joseph Heleluhe, on behalf of Liliʻuokalani
items.hawaiian: hoopau i na manao kuee mawaena o oukou
items.english_close: End the conflicting feelings among all of you.
items.feed_rendering: End the conflict among yourselves. Move together.
items.voice_evidence: The preserved phrase is a direct order to end internal conflict. In context, the dispute was interfering with unified anti-annexation petition work immediately before the September mass meeting.
items.source_label: Noenoe K. Silva, Aloha Betrayed, quoting the Sept. 1, 1897 Ebbitt House correspondence
items.translation_basis: Silva preserves the Hawaiian phrase and explains the political coordination context. No later newspaper publication date is inferred until direct issue evidence resolves it.
